current_example.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157173/assets/5fde287eaac0e3bdaaaa6d0c3b401e15ac732d25f3ec863dd6b11737e84d6fd3.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157173/assets/c7afb28995f6ee6a23b617b5201b107aa1acd652f66f64b1d6541de4adfcc23f.svg) Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{c}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 2+0\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
